tagline: The Colorado River back when it was only a brook.
intro: Out of Grand Lake the byway follows the young Colorado down by Granby to Hot Sulphur Springs, where the river goes into Byers Canyon, and on to Kremmling in the dry lower end of Middle Park. At Kremmling the pavement gives out. The rest is gravel, the county road along the south rim of Gore Canyon and on to State Bridge.

Downstream the Colorado waters and powers a good part of the Southwest. Up here, as the state's byway page has it, it is no different from dozens of other Rocky Mountain streams, a clear brook across meadows and down red rock gorges.

moments.title: Grand Lake
moments.text: The Utes called it Spirit Lake. Now water from Lake Granby is at times pumped back into it and sent under the Continental Divide to the eastern slope.

moments.title: Hot Sulphur Springs
moments.text: Spring water comes up at 125 degrees, and the town keeps Halloween on October 30, from when the 31st was payday and payday meant gunfights.

moments.title: Gore Canyon
moments.text: The gravel road keeps to the south rim. Below, in a roadless three-mile gorge with walls about 1,000 feet high, only the railroad and the whitewater boats get through.

practical: The road between Kremmling and State Bridge is gravel, with limited services.
